subject: Transcript: Former Apple cellular silicon program manager on in-house modem (C2) rollout, yields and Qualcomm share into 2027
body:
TAMARIND EXPERT NETWORK | Transcript Summary | Call date: Oct 12, 2026

Expert: Former Senior Program Manager, Cellular Silicon at Apple (left March 2026; 9 years in the modem and RF organization).
Interviewer: Tamarind client (buy-side)

Key takeaways (summary prepared by Tamarind; full transcript attached):

1. Where C2 stands. The in-house modem now ships in the base iPhone 18 and the iPad line. The expert said Apple's internal target for the 2027 iPhone cycle was to carry C2 in roughly half of all units, including some Pro models. In her last quarter at Apple, that target was "under review" because the Pro-tier carrier certification slipped.

2. Why the slip. Two issues: sub-6 throughput in dense urban deployments at two large U.S. carriers, and a wafer-level yield issue on the RF transceiver die that held effective supply below plan. "The base-model volumes were fine; the Pro-tier ask was a stretch."

3. Qualcomm exposure. She believes Qualcomm will keep supplying most Pro-tier modems through 2027, with Apple's modem content cost savings per unit coming in about $8-11 below what internal planning had assumed ($18-22 per unit at target mix).

4. Margin math. At full planned mix the expert said Finance had counted roughly 40-60bp of annual iPhone gross margin benefit from the modem swap. A mix reduction to approximately 30% of 2027 units would cut that to roughly 20-30bp.

5. Timing. She expects the target mix to be reset "around the Q1 planning cycle," and doesn't expect Apple to discuss it in the October call.

6. Confidence. Firm on the Pro certification issues and the yield problem, less sure on the final unit mix and on Apple's most recent decision, since she left in March.

Compliance: Expert confirmed no MNPI and no obligations breached.

Full transcript (17 pages) attached. Reply to schedule a follow-up call with this expert.
